review_type: Agent review of exact-match failures and evidence references
interpretation_limits: All exact-match scores remain authoritative for this preregistered pilot. These classifications were assigned after observing the outputs and must not replace those scores.
This is a Codex diagnostic review, not independently adjudicated human annotation, a new gold set, or a validated semantic-equivalence metric.
Representation and paraphrase mismatches are still violations of the requested exact output contract and may be unusable by a downstream configuration consumer.
No primary outcome or label file was modified. No API calls were made for this diagnostic.
qualitative_findings: All 27 value-string mismatches in completed answers appear to retain the intended current setting in context. No contradictory setting choice, adoption of a superseded value, or incorrect scope transfer was identified in this review.
One summary arm failed because a summary reached the configured output cap. Its three fields remain failures under the original metric; the partial summary is not a completed answer.

Four retrieval-arm evidence IDs, across two tasks whose values passed exact match, cite the update event for unchanged fields. These are objectively unsupported references under the public field-level decision protocol.
The current pilot does not establish a substantive constraint-retention advantage. Versioned and retrieval have identical task-level exact-match outcomes; the provenance observations are exploratory.
